title: Visa and Immigration FAQs | Unique Visa Services
description: Answers to common visa and immigration FAQs: regulation, fees, timescales, documents and how to start your application with Unique Visa Services.
intro: These visa and immigration FAQs answer the questions our clients ask most often.

faqs.q: Do I need an adviser, or can I apply myself?
faqs.a: You can apply directly. Many people use us because a missing document or misunderstood rule can mean a refusal, a lost fee and months of delay.

faqs.q: Do I need to visit your office?
faqs.a: No. You can meet us in Manchester, or we can work with you by phone, video call and email from anywhere in the UK.

faqs.q: How much do your services cost?
faqs.a: Our fee depends on the service and is agreed before we start. Government fees are paid separately. See our fees page.
Yes. We are registered with the Immigration Advice Authority, reference F200700144.

faqs.q: Can you guarantee my visa will be approved?
faqs.a: No adviser can guarantee a decision, as it is made by the Home Office or the embassy. What we can do is tell you honestly whether you qualify and make sure your application meets the rules, which gives you the best chance.

faqs.q: How do I check you are regulated?
faqs.a: Search for us on the Immigration Advice Authority’s online register using our reference number, shown at the bottom of every page.
Documents not in English or Welsh usually need a certified translation. We can arrange this or tell you exactly what is needed.

faqs.q: Where can I find visa and immigration FAQs for a specific visa?
faqs.a: Each visa page on our website has its own FAQs at the bottom, covering the questions clients ask about that visa.

sections.heading: About our service
sections.text:
We are regulated by the Immigration Advice Authority (IAA), the body that regulates immigration advisers in the UK. We help with UK visas, settlement and citizenship, sponsor licences for employers, and travel visas from the UK.

Our fee is agreed in writing before we start. Government, embassy and visa centre fees are paid separately, at cost.
